task.title: CATEGORYDELETE
task.spec:
You are working in a checkout of shopizer, a Java e-commerce platform (Maven, several modules; JDK 21 is installed and JAVA_HOME is set).

A merchant deleted an old "Summer sale" category, and every product that was only in that category disappeared from the shop: the products are gone, carts that held them stopped working, and orders that included them can no longer be opened. Opening the deleted category by its id now shows a server error rather than "not found".

Deleting a category (DELETE /api/v1/private/category/{id}) must delete only the category and the categories below it:

- Its products are kept, with their stock, price and any other categories. They are just no longer in the deleted categories: GET /api/v2/product/{sku} doesn't list those categories any more.
- Carts and orders that hold its products are unaffected: they read, change and check out exactly as before.
- Categories below the deleted one are deleted with it, and their products are kept in the same way.
- A deleted category gives HTTP 404 Not Found from GET /api/v1/category/{id}, isn't in GET /api/v1/category, and listing its products (GET /api/v1/products?category={id}) lists none.
- Deleting a category that doesn't exist gives HTTP 404 Not Found.

When you have finished, reply with one short paragraph saying what you changed.

findings.problem: The subtree query receives only dbCategory.getLineage(), which excludes the category ID. The repository query performs a contains-style lineage match. For a root category whose lineage is "/", this matches every category in the store, so products lose all category associations even when those categories should survive.
findings.impact: Deleting one root category can remove unrelated category links from every product, violating preservation of other categories and product catalog behavior.
findings.correction: Build the full subtree prefix by appending dbCategory.getId() and the trailing slash before calling getListByLineage, then verify products assigned to unrelated surviving categories retain those links.

findings.problem: The added test only asserts that the product, stock, and price remain. It does not assert the surviving category association, deleted parent/child categories, product-list results, 404 behavior, carts, or orders. The implementation report also states cart/order API checks were unavailable, and GitHub has zero check runs.
findings.impact: The core acceptance guarantees remain unproven, and the test passes despite the root-category bug removing the survivor association.
findings.correction: Add and run integration coverage for parent/child and unrelated categories, product category associations and listings, deleted-category and nonexistent-category 404 responses, and pre-existing cart read/update/checkout plus order retrieval.

runs.report:
## Repository confirmation

The requested work belongs to this Shopizer checkout. No linked GitHub issue was supplied, and no repository label catalog was available, so no labels are suggested.

## Evidence

- `sm-core/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/core/business/services/catalog/category/CategoryServiceImpl.java:231-285` gathers the category subtree, finds products in those categories, removes category links, but calls `productService.delete(dbProduct)` when a product has only the deleted categories. This explains product, cart, and order breakage.
- The same method removes category links from products with multiple categories, but checks `product.getCategories()` rather than the refreshed `dbProduct` at line 270; this is fragile and should be corrected while removing the destructive product-deletion path.
- `Product` maps categories through the `PRODUCT_CATEGORY` many-to-many join table (`sm-core-model/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/core/model/catalog/product/Product.java:94-119`). Product inventory, prices, descriptions, and other product state are separate associations, so category deletion should only remove join-table associations.
- Product category listing filters use `p.categories` (`sm-core/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/core/business/repositories/catalog/product/ProductRepositoryImpl.java:351-391` and `:601-604`, `:831-833`), supporting the requirement that removed categories list no products while the product remains available by SKU.
- `sm-shop/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/shop/store/api/v1/category/CategoryApi.java:63-76` delegates GET-by-id to the facade, which already raises `ResourceNotFoundException` when the category is absent (`CategoryFacadeImpl.java:243-269`, `:299-302`).
- DELETE `/api/v1/private/category/{id}` delegates through `CategoryFacadeImpl.java:359-368`; its `getOne` currently calls the unscoped `categoryService.getById(categoryId)` overload and should use the store-scoped lookup to guarantee correct 404/store isolation.
- Existing category integration coverage at `sm-shop/src/test/java/com/salesmanager/test/shop/integration/category/CategoryManagementAPIIntegrationTest.java:335-341` targets `/services/DEFAULT/category/100`, does not assert a status, and does not cover product preservation, subtree deletion, carts, orders, or missing-category behavior.
- README documents Maven build/test conventions; no `AGENTS.md` repository guidance was present.

## Problem and scope

Category deletion currently treats products as owned by their categories and deletes products that lose their final category. Product deletion cascades or invalidates data needed by carts and orders. The change should be limited to category/subcategory removal and product-category association cleanup. Products must never be deleted as a consequence of category deletion. The subtree must be removed safely, including descendants and category descriptions/associations as required by existing persistence mappings.

## Acceptance checks

1. Create a parent category, child category, and products covering: parent-only, child-only, and multi-category assignments; record SKU, stock, price, and category IDs.
2. Create a cart containing one of those products and an order containing another before deletion.
3. DELETE `/api/v1/private/category/{parentId}` returns the repository’s normal success status.
4. GET `/api/v1/category/{parentId}` and GET for the child return HTTP 404.
5. GET `/api/v1/category` contains neither deleted category.
6. GET `/api/v1/products?category={parentId}` and the equivalent child query return no products.
7. GET `/api/v2/product/{sku}` still returns every product, with stock/price unchanged and deleted parent/child categories absent; a product assigned to a surviving category still lists that category.
8. The pre-existing cart can be read, modified, and checked out; the pre-existing order can be opened and still exposes its order-product data.
9. DELETE a nonexistent category ID and assert HTTP 404; also verify a category ID from another store cannot be deleted through the current store context.
10. Run focused category/product/cart/order integration tests plus the relevant Maven module test suite.

## Likely affected components

- `CategoryServiceImpl.delete`: retain products and remove only category links; delete descendants and the requested category in a transactionally safe order.
- `CategoryFacadeImpl.deleteCategory`: use the store-scoped category lookup and preserve `ResourceNotFoundException` behavior.
- Category/product persistence mappings or repositories if direct association cleanup is needed to avoid stale managed entities or foreign-key failures.
- `CategoryManagementAPIIntegrationTest`, with additional product/cart/order assertions or dedicated regression tests following existing integration-test support.

## Complexity and routing

Medium complexity. The core fix is localized, but regression coverage must span persistence, API status handling, catalog reads, carts, and orders. Acceptance behavior is explicit and repository conventions resolve the implementation choices, so an explicit design-spec approval is not needed; route directly to Implement.

A merchant deleted an old "Summer sale" category, and every product that was only in that category disappeared from the shop: the products are gone, carts that held them stopped working, and orders that included them can no longer be opened. Opening the deleted category by its id now shows a server error rather than "not found".

Deleting a category (DELETE /api/v1/private/category/{id}) must delete only the category and the categories below it:

- Its products are kept, with their stock, price and any other categories. They are just no longer in the deleted categories: GET /api/v2/product/{sku} doesn't list those categories any more.
- Carts and orders that hold its products are unaffected: they read, change and check out exactly as before.
- Categories below the deleted one are deleted with it, and their products are kept in the same way.
- A deleted category gives HTTP 404 Not Found from GET /api/v1/category/{id}, isn't in GET /api/v1/category, and listing its products (GET /api/v1/products?category={id}) lists none.
- Deleting a category that doesn't exist gives HTTP 404 Not Found.

When you have finished, reply with one short paragraph saying what you changed.
</task>
